data.heading: What to bring to your first meeting with a lawyer
data.body:
A little preparation helps you make the most of a first meeting with a lawyer. Here's what to gather.

  • Any documents related to your matter: contracts, letters, notices or emails.
  • A short timeline of what happened and when.
  • Names and contact details of anyone else involved.
  • A list of questions you want to ask.
  • Notes about any deadlines you're aware of.

Don't worry if you don't have everything. The first meeting is mainly about understanding your situation and your options.

It also helps to think about what you'd like to happen. Knowing your goals lets the lawyer explain which routes may be open to you, and the likely costs and timescales involved.

Finally, ask how fees work and what happens next. A good lawyer will be happy to explain.

This article is general information, not legal advice. If you need help with your own situation, contact [Your Business Name] to arrange a consultation.

data.heading: Reading a contract before you sign: a few tips
data.body:
Contracts can be long and full of unfamiliar words. These general tips can help you understand what you're agreeing to.

Read the whole thing, not just the summary. Important details are often in the small print near the end.

Look for the key points: what each side has to do, how much is paid and when, how long the agreement lasts, and how it can be ended.

Watch for words like 'automatically renews', 'non-refundable' and 'penalty'. They often signal terms that matter.

If something is unclear, ask the other party to explain it in writing. If it's important, ask for it to be changed before you sign.

For larger or more complex agreements, it's often worth having a lawyer review it first.

Keep a signed copy of every contract somewhere safe, along with any emails that changed or explained its terms.

This article is general information and is not legal advice. For advice about a specific contract, speak to a qualified lawyer.
